text: Lice on pigs are blood-sucking, causing irritation and, in severe cases, anemia — about 3 mm long, found behind the ears, at the elbows, and between the legs; treat with Ivermectin (1 ml/30 kg) or Asuntol (1 g/liter of water). Mange spreads by contact (not transmissible to pigs from other species, nor to humans) and is worsened by daily washing that keeps the pen humid — the ideal condition for mange survival. Intense irritation causes vigorous scratching, ear shaking, red blisters, and dark ear crusting; affected pigs (especially young ones) eat poorly, grow slowly, and can develop secondary skin infection. Treat with subcutaneous Ivermectin twice within 12–14 days (1% Ivermectin: 1 ml per 30 kg), or Ivermectin mixed in feed for 7 days, or a harder-to-apply insecticide spray like Asuntol.
